module purpose: neorv32_cpu is a structural top level: it instantiates the instruction frontend, control unit, register file, ALU and load/store unit, and (by generics) the counters, PMP and inter-core communication units (lines 186-456), wires their ports together, packs the three machine interrupt inputs into irq_machine (line 276), ORs the extension CSR read values into xcsr_res (line 279) and the write-back sources into rf_wdata (line 330), and ties the outputs of units that are not built to constants (lines 305, 426, 427, 454, 455).

use-case flows.value: register operands driven by the register file to the ALU, the control unit and the LSU store-data input
register write-back data: ALU result, load data, CSR read data and ctrl.pc_ret ORed and delivered to the register file write input
ALU address result delivered as the load/store address, the PMP check address and a control-unit input
PMP fault decision on the access address delivered to the control unit and the LSU, or the constant '0' when no PMP is built
CSR read values of the counters, ALU, PMP and ICC units ORed into xcsr_res for the control unit, and the control unit's CSR read data returned toward write-back
machine, fast and debug interrupt requests presented to the control unit
ALU and LSU status delivered to the control unit: comparison result, completion, wait, error and the LSU's address value
CSR write and read commands, address and write data carried from the control record to the ICC unit
inter-core link data sent on icc_tx_o and received on icc_rx_i, or icc_terminate_c on icc_tx_o when ICC_EN is false
instruction fetch: the frontend's bus request and response, and the fetched-instruction record delivered to the control unit
control record driven by the control unit to every unit
data-memory access: the LSU's data-bus request and response
rstn_i distributed to every unit; what is cleared happens inside the units, which are not supplied

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt and debug-entry requests -- the request inputs the control unit receives as its machine, fast and debug interrupt requests
conceptual assets.reasoning: This entity reads msi_i, mei_i and mti_i to form `irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i;` (line 276; each port SOURCES irq_machine at occurrence 2) and wires that vector into the control unit (irq_machine_i, line 267); firq_i and dbi_i enter the control unit directly (CONNECTS irq_fast_i, line 268; CONNECTS irq_dbg_i, line 266). The control unit is not supplied, so integrity is Established as delivery: it must receive exactly the request bits present on these inputs (lines 266-268, 276). Each port is where its request enters this entity on its way to a consumer that is not supplied, so each sets the concept. irq_machine computes the 3-bit request vector: its record is DERIVES_FROM mei_i, msi_i, mti_i (occurrence 3), a combination of three requests rather than a COPIES of one, and it is the only element holding the vector the control unit receives. Availability is not claimed: the assignment and connections are continuous, and whether a request must be taken is decided inside the control unit. Confidentiality is not established: no line restricts who observes these inputs. clk_i and rstn_i are excluded as clock and reset inputs (wired to every unit's clk_i and rstn_i, lines 192-193 and others).

conceptual assets.concept: Register source operands -- the values the register file returns for the instruction being executed
conceptual assets.reasoning: The register file instance drives rs1, rs2 and rs3 (rs1_o line 324, rs2_o line 325, rs3_o line 326). rs1 feeds the control unit (rf_rs1_i, line 262) and the ALU (rs1_i, line 364); rs2 feeds the ALU (rs2_i, line 365) and the LSU store-data input (wdata_i, line 387); rs3 feeds the ALU (rs3_i, line 366). Producer and consumers are all units that are not supplied, so integrity is Established as delivery: the ALU, LSU and control unit must receive exactly the operands the register file drives (lines 262, 324-326, 364-366, 387). Each signal is the only element of this entity that carries its operand ('storage': not assigned only means the unit drives it), so each computes through its CONNECTS edge of mode out. rs3 carries a register value only when the register file is built with RS3_EN => rf_rs3_en_c (line 315), that is RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu or RISCV_ISA_Zfinx (line 95); what the unit drives otherwise is inside the register file. Confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Register write-back data -- the result value written into the register file
conceptual assets.reasoning: `rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;` (line 330) is the computation this entity performs on the result path, and rf_wdata is wired into the register file's rd_i (line 323). The register file is not supplied, so integrity is Established: it must receive exactly the OR of the four sources defined at line 330. rf_wdata computes the merged value (DERIVES_FROM alu_res, occurrence 3). alu_res (ALU res_o, line 369) and lsu_rdata (LSU rdata_o, line 388) are where the ALU result and the loaded data first exist in this entity, and each SOURCES rf_wdata (line 330), so each computes through its CONNECTS edge of mode out. csr_rdata, the third source, is listed under the CSR read-data concept. ctrl.pc_ret is a field of the ctrl record that only receives the control unit's output (line 253) and is read here as data (line 330), so it is a carrier under the sub-unit wiring rule; dbus_rsp_i, through which the LSU receives load data (line 395), is a transport record. Availability is context-dependent: when a register write happens is decided inside the register file and control unit.

conceptual assets.concept: CSR read data -- control and status register values read back by the CPU
conceptual assets.reasoning: `xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc;` (line 279) merges the CSR read values of the counters unit (rdata_o, line 299), the ALU (csr_o, line 371), the PMP (csr_o, line 416) and the ICC unit (csr_rdata_o, line 445), and the result is wired into the control unit's xcsr_rdata_i (line 264). The control unit drives csr_rdata (csr_rdata_o, line 263), which SOURCES rf_wdata (line 330). All producers and consumers are units that are not supplied, so integrity is Established as delivery: the control unit must receive exactly the OR at line 279, and the write-back path exactly the value on csr_rdata. xcsr_res computes the merge (DERIVES_FROM xcsr_cnt, occurrence 3); each xcsr_* source and csr_rdata computes through its CONNECTS edge of mode out. Configuration: xcsr_cnt comes from the counters unit only when RISCV_ISA_Zicntr or RISCV_ISA_Zihpm (line 285), else it is (others => '0') (line 305); xcsr_pmp only when RISCV_ISA_Smpmp (line 402), else zero (line 426); xcsr_icc only when ICC_EN (line 434), else zero (line 454). The zero tie-offs keep a unit that is not built from contributing to the OR. Confidentiality is not established: no line in this file restricts which CSR may be read.

conceptual assets.concept: Load/store access address -- the address the ALU computes for a memory access, used by the LSU, checked by the PMP, and reported back by the LSU
conceptual assets.reasoning: The ALU's add_o drives alu_add (line 370), which is wired to the LSU address input (addr_i, line 386), to the PMP check address (addr_ls_i, line 418, present when RISCV_ISA_Smpmp, line 402) and to the control unit (alu_add_i, line 261). The LSU drives lsu_mar (mar_o, line 389) into the control unit (lsu_mar_i, line 271). All are units that are not supplied, so integrity is Established as delivery: the LSU and the PMP must receive the same address the ALU computes (lines 386, 418), and the control unit exactly the value the LSU reports (line 271). alu_add and lsu_mar each compute through their CONNECTS edge of mode out. The PMP's decision on this address is a separate concept (pmp_fault). Confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Memory-protection fault decision -- whether the PMP flags the current load/store access
conceptual assets.reasoning: When RISCV_ISA_Smpmp (line 402), the PMP unit receives the access address alu_add (addr_ls_i, line 418) and the control record (line 414) and drives pmp_fault (fault_o, line 420); pmp_fault is wired into both the control unit (pmp_fault_i, line 257) and the LSU (pmp_fault_i, line 392). When the PMP is not built, `pmp_fault <= '0';` (line 427) fixes the decision at a constant. Both consumers are not supplied, so integrity is Established: the LSU and the control unit must receive exactly the decision the PMP computes, or the constant of line 427 in builds without a PMP. An element whose value is a permission result computes it; pmp_fault does so through the CONNECTS edge of mode out (occurrence 4). Availability: the connection delivers the decision continuously; how the consumers act on it is not visible here, so no further claim is made. Confidentiality is not established.

conceptual assets.concept: Load/store error status -- the error indication the LSU reports to the control unit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The LSU drives lsu_err (err_o, line 391), a 4-bit value wired only into the control unit (lsu_err_i, line 272). The LSU also receives pmp_fault (line 392) and the data-bus response (line 395), but how it forms err_o is inside a unit that is not supplied, so no internal computation is claimed. Integrity is Established as delivery: the control unit must receive exactly the status the LSU drives (lines 272, 391). An error flag computes its decision; lsu_err does so through its CONNECTS edge of mode out.

conceptual assets.concept: ALU comparison result -- the 2-bit comparison decision the ALU delivers to the control unit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The ALU, which receives the operands rs1 and rs2 (lines 364-365), drives alu_cmp (cmp_o, line 368), and alu_cmp is wired only into the control unit (alu_cmp_i, line 260). A comparison result is a decision, so the element carrying it computes it. The control unit is not supplied, so integrity is Established as delivery: it must receive exactly the value the ALU computes (lines 260, 368). What the control unit decides from it is not visible here.

conceptual assets.concept: Execution-unit progress status -- the ALU completion and LSU wait indications the control unit receives
conceptual assets.reasoning: The ALU drives alu_cp_done (done_o, line 373) into the control unit (alu_cp_done_i, line 259), and the LSU drives lsu_wait (wait_o, line 390) into the control unit (lsu_wait_i, line 270). Both are single-bit status values whose producer and consumer are not supplied, so integrity is Established as delivery: the control unit must receive exactly the status each unit drives. Each computes through its CONNECTS edge of mode out. Availability is not claimed: whether the control unit must eventually advance on these values depends on behavior outside this file.

conceptual assets.concept: Inter-core communication data -- the values this CPU sends to and receives from another core over the ICC link
conceptual assets.reasoning: When ICC_EN (line 434), the ICC unit receives CSR commands from the control record (lines 441-444), drives icc_tx_o directly (line 447) and consumes icc_rx_i (line 448). When ICC_EN is false (line 453), `icc_tx_o <= icc_terminate_c;` (line 455) ties the output to a named constant and icc_rx_i is unused. The icc_t record (fields rdy, ack, dat) carries a data word with a handshake and no address, byte enables or read/write distinction, so it is not a transport record under section 7. The value leaves the entity through icc_tx_o and enters through icc_rx_i, so integrity is Established by the boundary assumption: the receiver must get exactly the value the ICC unit drives, and the ICC unit exactly the value on icc_rx_i. icc_tx_o is an exit port (CONNECTS from neorv32_cpu_icc_inst.icc_tx_o, occurrence 2); icc_rx_i sets the received value (CONNECTS mode in to neorv32_cpu_icc_inst.icc_rx_i, occurrence 2). The ctrl.csr_* fields that carry the CSR commands only pass the control unit's output to the ICC unit, so they are carriers. Confidentiality is not established: no line restricts the link.

conceptual assets.concept: Control-record commands -- the control word the control unit drives to every other unit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control unit drives the ctrl record (ctrl_o, line 253), and the frontend, counters, register file, ALU, LSU and PMP receive it whole (lines 194, 297, 321, 362, 384, 414); the ICC unit receives four of its fields (lines 441-444), and ctrl.pc_ret is read into rf_wdata (line 330). Integrity is Established as delivery to consumers that are not supplied. No reference is listed, as a mapping limitation: ctrl is a whole internal record, and each of its fields only receives the control unit's output or passes it unchanged to a unit (no field is tested in an if, case or when condition, and ctrl.pc_ret is only read as data), so the fields are carriers under section 7; the remaining fields have no local use in the map. Reporting the whole record would bypass that restriction.

conceptual assets.concept: Fetched instruction stream -- the instruction record the frontend delivers to the control unit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The frontend unit drives ibus_req_o and receives ibus_rsp_i (lines 196-197) and drives the frontend record (frontend_o, line 199), which the control unit receives (frontend_i, line 255). Integrity is Established as delivery to a consumer that is not supplied. No reference is listed, as a mapping limitation: ibus_req_o and ibus_rsp_i are transport records (request fields addr, data, ben, stb, rw; response fields ack, err, data), and frontend is a whole internal record whose fields only carry the frontend's output to the control unit, so they are carriers. dbus_req_o and dbus_rsp_i (lines 394-395) are excluded as transport for the same reason.
